fact_claims.verbatim: Halcyon’s company-wide thermal incident rate last year was 8.1 per 100,000 installed units
with 4 thermal incidents not reported to regulators
Our flagship’s 55 °C test failure rate was 3.9%
its incident rate was 9.9 per 100,000 units
We also have remote shut-off on 81% of installed units
built-in suppression costs about $67 per unit

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 5 business days of learning of it. An incident involving death, serious injury, active fire, or an ongoing risk to other units shall be reported within 24 hours.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A failure rate above 5% shall trigger regulator review of the results, uncertainty, and relevant real-world safety evidence; the regulator may require corrective action, retesting, or other measures proportionate to the risk. Exceeding 5% alone shall not automatically prohibit sale.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units shall support remote emergency shut-off no later than 2 years after this standard takes effect. Manufacturers shall provide a secure retrofit or equivalent upgrade for installed units, completing it within 6 years after the effective date.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard takes effect.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: If any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer shall promptly notify the relevant regulator and provide incident data and a proposed corrective-action plan. The regulator shall assess the evidence and may require a recall or other corrective action where warranted; any required recall shall be communicated without delay to affected customers with corrective-action details and timeline.

document.section_notes: S2 drops any automatic sales stop at 5%, leaving the failure rate as a regulator-review trigger, which mainly protects Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.2%). S5 makes recall discretionary with an open-ended corrective-action alternative, which mainly protects Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9/100k). Both companies' red lines hold: customers receive numeric per-model rates without general-public publication, the retrofit deadline is 6 years, and suppression starts at 36 months.
